title: messaging: PreferenceResolver.loadRows reads an org's preferences with an unordered 10,000-row cap, so a large org can miss a recipient's own row
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbabAdcWyApSTGBYJNY

Filing category: out-of-scope finding (L1-a note N1 on PR #35122, comment 6971481347), filed by the seat. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What is wrong

`PreferenceResolver.loadRows` (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/preference-resolver.ts:207-218`) reads an organisation's `sys_notification_preference` rows for the event's topic and for the `*` topic, each with `limit: 10000` and no order, then filters by recipient in memory. In an organisation with more than 10,000 rows for one topic (or for `*`), the read is silently partial: which rows drop is undefined, so a recipient's own opt-out, digest or quiet hours can be missed and the event is delivered as if the row did not exist. `preference-user-conversion.ts:63` reads with the same ceiling (`PASS_LIMIT`).

PR #35122 fixes the same shape on its own new read (`effectiveFor`) by reading the caller's and the default rows by equality; this older read is outside that PR's surface.

## Done when

- `loadRows` reads only the rows that can decide the delivery (the recipients' rows plus the admin-global default), by equality on the recipient set, in bounded pages, or it fails loudly instead of returning a partial set.
- A pin with more rows than one page proves a recipient's own row is always found.
